correctness.rationale: The source string is interpreted using the paper\'s explicit descending-coefficient convention and generates a \(4096\)-word negacyclic ideal. Its \(2\)-torsion has size \(1024\), recovering type \(4^2 2^8\), and exhaustive Lee enumeration recovers distance \(16\). The Gray image has \(4096\) words and binary span dimension \(12\), so it is exactly linear. Direct coordinate-permutation and polynomial calculations identify its degree-\(60\) binary cyclic generator. Column-dependency enumeration proves dual distance \(4\). The packaged standard-library verifier reconstructs every finite step and returns VERIFY_OK.

value.rationale: The source singles out this code as a record-breaking \(\mathbb Z_4\) negacyclic construction and explicitly motivates binary Gray images while noting that they are generally nonlinear. Determining that this particular record has a fully linear Gray image is therefore a meaningful structural classification rather than a routine restatement of its Lee distance. The exact binary cyclic generator, full weight enumerator, dual distance, rank, and kernel together give a reusable fingerprint and show that this quaternary record can be handled by ordinary binary cyclic-code algebra. The result is not sold as a binary-distance record.
